conclusions: Every directed stream acknowledges about49frames/s in both runs; explicit one-frame/ACK serialization and a20ms injected RTT yield an ideal50frames/s ceiling. This is evidence of a frame-service ceiling, including under low transaction load.
Both input rates use100ms producer cadence and about10BATCHframes/s per directed stream; changing transactions per batch changes payload volume without eliminating control-frame pressure.

Approximately60directed controlframes/proposedround and12streams predict about8rounds/s after reserving10BATCHframes/s/stream. Observed round progress is about7.8/s. This is an aggregate consistency check, not a per-transaction path decomposition.
No FETCH/DATA is sent during either entire trial, and boundary materialization queues are empty. The recorded runs do not implicate payload-repair traffic as a latency source.

700ms main timeout is configured, but positive CER/commit transitions can complete before expiry. The current archives cannot show how many expiries changed an Open outcome to NoCer or lay on a transaction critical path.
limitations: Only two completed trials are audited:40tx/s preflight and first1000tx/s matrix trial, not the final matrix population.

Boundary snapshots are partial observations of continuous operation. Queue depths are endpoint samples, not means/maxima or proof of continuously nonempty queues. Per-replica windows differ slightly; message ratios can straddle different round boundaries.
Latency is a completion-window population at each origin, including transactions inserted before the window. It is not an arrival cohort or an all-replica barrier.

Zero retries and ACK failures means zero deltas in these Delugi application-transport counters over the audited measurement windows. It does not measure kernel TCP retransmissions or establish any corresponding property for other protocols.

No stage-level timeline is retained in sustained mode: round admission, main/catchup arms/expiries, observations/input-ready, direct-commit, ordering release and materialization events are filtered from stdout; compact snapshots omit their maps.
Generator schedule lag is a cumulative maximum at the window endpoint, not a measurement-window percentile or a direct handler/queue latency measurement.

This audit does not attribute a numerical fraction of the758–782ms means to transport, timers, construction, signature checking, scanner release or local materialization; same-run correlation is not an intervention.
